Welcome to Crockenhill Primary School
Our village school was built in 1906, and added to in 2011 to provide a welcoming, happy and safe environment in which our children thrive. We are a one form entry school, with the ability to accommodate 210 pupils from the village and further afield. As well as seven classrooms and hall, we also have a dedicated area for our ICT suite and a well-stocked library. There is also an art room which our pupils use regularly.

Kent's Kids!
BBC Radio Kent came to visit our school to record some of our Year 4 pupils to take part in the Kent's Kids competition!
We are so excited to hear some familiar voices on the BBC Radio Kent Breakfast Show this week. Some of our Year 4 pupils will be giving listeners a series of clues to a mystery object. Tune in between 7:30am and 8:30am Monday to Thursday to see if you can guess the unknown object!

We celebrated Science Week across the school with our exciting theme "Curiosity - What's your question?". The aim of the week was to encourage children to think like scientists by asking thoughtful questions about the world around them.

120 Birthday Celebrations
On Friday 3rd July, our school community came together to celebrate 120 years of Crockenhill Primary School with an afternoon full of fun at our family picnic. The sun shone on the school field, where families and staff gathered together to enjoy the celebrations surrounded by bunting designed by all of the children.

Harvest Celebrations!
On Thursday we celebrated Harvest at school with an assembly filled with songs and a visit from Pastor Mark from Crockenhill Baptist Church. The very kind donations from our school community will support the valuable work of Swanley Food Bank.

pageCache.text:
Remote Learning when school is closed, or partially closed due to weather conditions
Should the decision be made by the Headteacher to close or restrict attendance at school due to severe weather conditions which could put pupils or staff at risk, or the inability to get to school due to transport difficulties, school be will providing continued learning at home for all classes. Children who can get to school when it is partially open will access the same learning as those at home. It may, however, be necessary to shorten the school day in order to allow the staff to get to and from school safely.
At Crockenhill Primary School, we will be providing this home learning via:
More links are available for each class in our sections:

Meet the CASPERS Team
BREAKFAST CLUB
Breakfast Club has been running for several years now and is well established and very popular. It has a great atmosphere and is a place where children can meet with their friends before school and enjoy a healthy breakfast together. It runs from 7.30 am - 9.00 am every morning , term time only. We close the doors to breakfast club promptly at 8.30 am. The cost is £4.00 per child per session for prebooked and £5 for on the day bookings. You are welcome to just drop in on the day for Breakfast Club without booking.
After School Club
After school club is provided by the team everyday from end of school to 5:45pm. Pre booking is essential via a Booking form at £9 per session. These are available on the Website, from the office or Mrs Bradley. On the day bookings can be taken if there is space - spaces are limited. Please call Caspers on 07436289735 to see if a space is available on the day bookings are charged at £12. All payment is made via the school gateway.

pageCache.pageTitle: Crockenhill Primary School - School Opening Hours
pageCache.text:
School Opening Hours
Crockenhill Primary School operates a soft start system, whereby children have a 10 minute window from 8.40 am to 8.50 am to arrive in school. Morning registration takes place at 8.55 am.
Afternoon registration is 12.45 - 1pm for EYFS and KS1 and 1.15pm - 1.30pm for KS2
The day finishes at 3:20pm for EYFS and KS1 and at 3:25pm for KS2.
Total school hours in a typical week - KS1 - 32hrs 30 mins/KS2 - 32hrs 55 mins
The school opens at 8.40 am and closes at 3.30pm. This does not account for CASPERS - our wrap around care provision.
School Opening Hours

Young Voices 2026
Our School Choir visited the O2 to sing with thousands of other children at the Young Voices concert.
Our children sang their hearts out at the O2 arena. They had been rehearsing for weeks and gave a wonderful performance.
We are so proud of them!

pageCache.pageTitle: Crockenhill Primary School - NSPCC Number Day
pageCache.text:
NSPCC Number Day
On 6th February we celebrated Number Day at Crockenhill and raised over £100 for the NSPCC!
Our day was spent on a range of maths-based activities and to fundraise for the NSPCC we dressed as a digit! There was a real maths buzz around the school and it was a joy to see the children taking great pleasure in maths.
